description: The code a Map Edits node writes from its edit list and reads back (#662, utils/editFeatures/editFeatures.ts). `ops`: the edits the node makes, in order, as editFeatures.ts (EDIT_OPS) and curio_edit_features (OPS) list them. Jest checks editFeaturesCode writes each case's `code` from its `settings`, `circles` (1 when absent) and `comments` (the node's own lines when absent), that readEditFeaturesCode reads it back as those and that the code it then writes is the same, reads each `read` code as its `settings`, `circles` and `comments`, and refuses each `refused` code with `problem`, the whole text it says. utk_curio/sandbox/tests/test_feature_edits_code.py checks the sandbox's reader (utk_curio/sandbox/util/feature_edits_code.py) reads every code the same way, word for word, and writes each case with no `settings` and no `comments` as a new node's code (new_node_code), and utk_curio/sandbox/tests/test_feature_edits.py runs each `cases` code with curio_edit_features, checking the buildings left (`kept`).

cases.name: a new node: no edits, so the input is handed on as it came
cases.code:
# Map Edits writes this code from its edit list: each edit, in the
# order it was made, on the features whose key is one of its ids. It is
# written again when the list changes.
return curio_edit_features(input_0, [])

cases.name: two buildings removed, by their building_id, from one layer of several
cases.code:
# Map Edits writes this code from its edit list: each edit, in the
# order it was made, on the features whose key is one of its ids. It is
# written again when the list changes.
return curio_edit_features(input_0, [
    {"op": "remove", "ids": [1, 3]},
], key="building_id", layer="table_osm_buildings")

cases.name: a value set, a removal, then the removal put back
cases.code:
# Map Edits writes this code from its edit list: each edit, in the
# order it was made, on the features whose key is one of its ids. It is
# written again when the list changes.
return curio_edit_features(input_0, [
    {"op": "set", "ids": [2], "column": "name", "value": "Tower \"B\""},
    {"op": "remove", "ids": [3]},
    {"op": "restore", "ids": [3]},
    {"op": "set", "ids": [1], "column": "height", "value": None},
], key="building_id", layer="table_osm_buildings")

cases.name: a Map Edits log: a raise, a removal switched off and a removal by condition
cases.code:
# Map Edits writes this code from its edit list: each edit, in the
# order it was made, on the features whose key is one of its ids. It is
# written again when the list changes.
return curio_edit_features(input_0, [
    {"op": "offset", "ids": [2], "column": "height", "value": 3, "label": "Raise the tower"},
    {"op": "remove", "ids": [1], "label": "First building", "enabled": False},
    {"op": "remove", "where": "building_id >= 3"},
], key="building_id", layer="table_osm_buildings")

cases.name: a scale where a condition holds, and a value computed by an expression
cases.code:
# Map Edits writes this code from its edit list: each edit, in the
# order it was made, on the features whose key is one of its ids. It is
# written again when the list changes.
return curio_edit_features(input_0, [
    {"op": "scale", "where": "height > 11", "column": "height", "value": 0.5},
    {"op": "expr", "ids": [3], "column": "height", "value": "10 * 2"},
], key="building_id", layer="table_osm_buildings")

cases.name: a new layer of points, a point drawn into it, and a building removed
cases.code:
# Map Edits writes this code from its edit list: each edit, in the
# order it was made, on the features whose key is one of its ids. It is
# written again when the list changes.
return curio_edit_features(input_0, [
    {"op": "add", "layer": "cooling_centers", "id": "new-1", "geometry": {"type": "Point", "coordinates": [3, 3]}, "values": {"name": "Library"}},

cases.name: two circles, every input handed to the step, the edit naming its layer and that layer its id column
cases.code:
# Map Edits writes this code from its edit list: each edit, in the
# order it was made, on the features whose key is one of its ids. It is
# written again when the list changes.
return curio_edit_features([input_0, input_1], [
    {"op": "remove", "layer": "table_osm_buildings", "ids": [1]},
], keys={"table_osm_buildings": "building_id"}, by_input=True)
